fields.meta_description: Landing page SEO from a prompt: intent-led copy, title tags, schema, internal links and a lead form on a page you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Landing Page SEO Into Pages That Rank and Convert
fields.hero_description: Describe the offer and the query it should rank for. Emergent builds an indexable page with the title tag, headings, schema and a lead form, as code you own.
fields.features_heading: What Every SEO Landing Page Gets
fields.features_subheading: Landing page SEO gets a page ranking for the query its buyers search, then turns that organic visit into a lead or a sale.
fields.feature_1:
Title tag, meta and H1 from the query

Name the query and Emergent writes the title tag, meta description and H1 around it, each sized to show in full on a results page. Change the wording later with one prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Sections that follow search intent

The page opens with the answer the searcher came for, then uses H2s for the questions they ask next. The form sits after the first answer, where it reads as the next step.
fields.feature_3:
Schema, canonical tag and sitemap

Product, Breadcrumb or LocalBusiness schema is written into the page as JSON-LD. Each page gets a canonical tag and a sitemap entry, so crawlers index the version you meant.
fields.feature_4:
A mobile layout that loads copy first

The layout is responsive from the first build. Images carry alt text and fixed dimensions, and scripts load after the content, so a phone shows the headline before anything else.
fields.feature_5:
Every lead saved with its landing URL

Each form submission is saved to a database you own with the landing URL, referrer and UTM tags attached, then sent on to HubSpot or Slack. Organic leads stay separate from paid.
fields.feature_6:
Markup you can audit and keep

The page, its tags and its form export to your GitHub repository. Run any crawler against it, hand it to a developer, or host it somewhere else without rebuilding a thing.

fields.usecase_heading: SEO Landing Pages for Four Kinds of Query
fields.tab_content_1:
Rank a feature page for the query buyers type

A feature page targets one commercial query, such as shift scheduling software, with the title tag, H1 and first paragraph written around it. The answer comes first, a demo form follows it, and each request lands in your database with the landing URL.
fields.tab_content_2:
Publish one page per city, each with its own copy

City pages target searches like movers in Denver. Each city gets its own H1, service area, crew photos and LocalBusiness schema, so no two pages read as duplicates. Quote requests are saved with the city attached and posted to that branch's Slack channel.
fields.tab_content_3:
Answer the comparison search with a fair table

Comparison pages answer queries like Acme vs Globex or Globex alternatives. The page lays out the differences in a table, links to the feature pages it mentions, and ends with a trial signup that records which comparison the visitor read.
fields.tab_content_4:
Turn a template search into a captured lead

Template pages rank for queries like content calendar template. The page previews the template, explains how to fill it in, and asks for an email before the download. Every download is stored with its source page and synced to HubSpot.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an SEO Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Pick one query, match what already ranks for it, then build the tags, copy and links around it. Seven steps from keyword to an indexed page that converts.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Match what the top results deliver
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write the title tag, H1 and URL
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Answer before you ask for anything
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the single query the page should rank for and check that the top results are pages like yours. If the first page of Google is all guides, a sales page will struggle there; write a guide-shaped page or pick another query.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open the top ten and note what they share: format, depth and the questions they answer. A commercial query wants pricing and proof near the top. An informational one wants the definition first and the offer after it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the query in the title tag, the H1 and a short URL, worded the way people search it. Keep the title under 60 characters, and write a meta description that says what the page delivers, not a slogan.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Cover the topic at the depth the search needs: what it is, how it works, what it costs and the common questions. Place the form after the first answer, so visitors and crawlers both reach the content before the ask.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add schema, alt text and internal links
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add the structured data that fits the page, such as Product, Breadcrumb or LocalBusiness. Give every image descriptive alt text, and link to the page from related pages on your site with anchor text that names its topic.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test the page on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Load the page on a mid-range phone and run it through PageSpeed Insights. Compress the hero image, set image dimensions and defer scripts the first screen does not need. Fix layout shift before you publish.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish on your domain, keep the page indexable and submit the URL in Google Search Console. Track impressions, clicks and form conversions for the query each week, and rewrite the title when clicks lag the position.
